feedback.worked_solution:
We want to find a "path" from $R$ to $P$ consisting only of the vectors $a,d,$ and $c.$

According to the triangle law of addition,

$$
\overset{\to }{RP}=\overset{\to }{RQ}+\overset{\to }{QP}
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14040990/assets/b6eb4bdf68dcecd124ec7129b94b6c5adccc826f505ecda653069640efa439e2.png)

 

Now, from the original diagram, we have that

$$
\overset{\to }{RQ}=d,\,\overset{\to }{QP}=a.
$$

Let's add these to our diagram.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14040990/assets/90749b45c5e992ba17f09c6a3597adebcdad2ab9d354b2aee7e41058af69863a.png)

 

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{RP} & =\overset{\to }{RQ}+\overset{\to }{QP} \\  & =d+a.\end{aligned}
$$
